title: Step Supporting Validator Unit Lifecycle Contract

scope.purpose: Define reusable lifecycle obligations for a concrete Step Supporting Validator Unit instance, independently of the lifetimes of its associations and retained validation evidence.
scope.appliesTo: A concrete Step specialization that provisions or otherwise admits one or more Step Supporting Validator Unit instances.

terminology.validatorUnitInstance: One concrete runtime realization of a Step Supporting Validator Unit, identified independently of its associations and validation invocations.
terminology.instanceLifecycle: The progression of the validator-unit instance from provisioning/admission through availability, use, optional retention, and eventual release.
terminology.associationLifetime: The validity interval of one association between a validator-unit instance and one Step-defined target scope. It is governed by the Association Contract and is not the instance lifecycle.
terminology.evidenceRetentionLifetime: The period for which validation results, invocation records, and provenance remain retained and interpretable. It is governed by the concrete Step result/evidence policy and is not the instance lifecycle.
terminology.admission: The Step Composition decision that makes a provisioned and sufficiently prepared validator-unit instance eligible for use within the owning Step. Admission is not an association and does not itself invoke the unit.
terminology.release: The lifecycle action that ends the owning Step's right and ability to use the validator-unit instance and discharges the instance's runtime-resource obligations according to its specialized lifecycle.

independentLifetimes: The validator-unit instance lifecycle is independent of the lifetime of each association in which the instance participates.
The validator-unit instance lifecycle is independent of the retention lifetime of validation results, invocation evidence, and historical association provenance.
Ending an association does not by itself release, dispose, or invalidate the validator-unit instance.
Retaining historical results or provenance does not by itself require the validator-unit runtime instance to remain alive or callable.
Releasing the validator-unit instance does not authorize deletion or rewriting of retained results, invocation evidence, or historical association descriptors.
optionalityAndSpecialization: A Step is not required to select, provision, or admit a validator-unit instance.
The common contract defines lifecycle responsibilities and safety constraints, not a mandatory implementation state machine.
The concrete Step defines the actual lifecycle policy, required phases, transitions, reuse rules, and release conditions consistent with this contract.
Different validator-unit implementations may require different provisioning, initialization, readiness, shutdown, and release procedures.
compositionAuthority: The owning Step Composition coordinates and is authoritative for admitting, making available, retaining for reuse, quiescing, and releasing validator-unit instances within the Step.

A validator unit may implement or internally perform its own initialization and shutdown mechanics, but those mechanics do not transfer lifecycle policy or admission/release authority away from Step Composition.
An SPU that is an association target does not acquire lifecycle ownership or authority over the validator-unit instance.
No Pipeline-wide manager, global lifecycle service, or central mediator is required by this contract.

requirements: validatorUnitIdentity identifies one concrete validator-unit runtime instance within the identity scope defined by the owning Step specialization.
The identity remains stable for the lifetime of that instance, including periods in which the instance has no active associations or is retained for reuse.
A new runtime instance receives a distinct validatorUnitIdentity even when it uses the same implementation, configuration, or underlying resource category as a released instance.
Association identity and validator invocation identity are distinct from validatorUnitIdentity.

An instance identity is not a memory address, operating-system handle, resource identifier, or generation number unless the concrete Step explicitly defines a separate mapping and preserves the identity requirements.

Historical results and evidence may continue to reference validatorUnitIdentity after the runtime instance has been released; such a reference is historical identity, not proof that the instance remains alive.
lifecycleIdentity.replacement: Replacing a released, failed, or otherwise unusable instance with another runtime instance creates a new instance identity. The replacement may inherit configuration or logical role, but it must not impersonate the previous instance identity.

StepComposition: Determine whether the concrete Step requires a validator-unit instance and select the required specialized implementation/configuration.
Coordinate provisioning or acquisition of an instance through the mechanism selected by the concrete Step.
Coordinate required initialization and determine whether the instance satisfies the Step-defined readiness criteria.
Admit the instance into the Step's internal composition before making it eligible for association or invocation.
Maintain the authoritative instance identity and lifecycle/admission state needed for safe coordination.
Determine whether and under what conditions the instance may be reused, shared across associations, or invoked concurrently.
Prevent new invocations when the instance is not admitted, is quiescing, has failed, or has been released.
Coordinate quiescence and reconcile active invocations before release, subject to the concrete Step's cancellation and recovery policies.
Ensure all live associations are ended or otherwise made unusable before releasing the instance.
Coordinate the instance-specific shutdown and release procedure and record its outcome.
Keep instance release independent from the retention and interpretation of already-produced results and evidence.
StepSupportingValidatorUnit: Expose or satisfy the lifecycle capabilities and readiness requirements declared by its specialized behavioral/lifecycle realization.
Perform its implementation-specific initialization, readiness checks, quiescence, and shutdown mechanics when invoked or coordinated under its contract.
Report lifecycle failures or inability to accept work to Step Composition without independently changing its admission or association state.
Reject or safely fail invocations that violate its declared readiness, concurrency, or shutdown conditions.
Preserve the integrity of results already produced and returned according to its result and custody contracts.
SPU: May be associated with a validator-unit instance as a target scope.
Does not provision, admit, initialize, retain, quiesce, shut down, or release the validator-unit instance by virtue of being its association target.
May report target-specific constraints or request that Step Composition reconsider validator availability; such a report does not itself change lifecycle state.
StageComposition: Invokes the owning Step through the Step contract and does not directly manage the lifecycle of internal validator-unit instances.
Pipeline: Does not impose a global validator-unit instance lifecycle or own individual Step validator-unit runtime instances under this contract.

lifecyclePhases.nature: The following are conceptual lifecycle milestones, not a mandatory enum, linear state machine, or requirement that every implementation materialize each phase as a separate state.

phases.name: ProvisionedOrAcquired
phases.meaning: A concrete runtime instance has been created, obtained, or otherwise made available to the Step's lifecycle coordination.
phases.entryAuthority: Step Composition coordinates the acquisition/provisioning outcome.
constraints: Provisioning does not by itself establish readiness or authorize invocation.
The concrete Step defines whether provisioning creates a new instance or obtains a reusable instance from a Step-scoped source.

phases.name: Prepared
phases.meaning: The implementation-specific initialization and preparation required for the instance have completed sufficiently for readiness evaluation.
phases.entryAuthority: The validator implementation performs its preparation mechanics; Step Composition coordinates and observes completion.
constraints: Preparation requirements are validator-implementation-specific.
Partial or failed preparation must not be treated as readiness.

phases.name: Ready
phases.meaning: The instance satisfies the concrete Step's declared prerequisites for admission and intended use.
phases.entryAuthority: Step Composition determines readiness according to the specialized readiness criteria and available evidence.
constraints: Ready does not mean admitted, associated, or currently executing.
Readiness may be invalidated by implementation-specific conditions; the concrete Step defines detection and response.

phases.name: Admitted
phases.meaning: Step Composition has accepted the instance into the Step's internal composition and may establish associations or authorize invocations according to the other applicable contracts.
constraints: Admission is a Step-level eligibility decision and is distinct from association with any target.
An admitted instance may have zero, one, or multiple associations as permitted by the Association Contract specialization.
Admission alone does not require immediate invocation.

phases.name: AvailableOrInUse
phases.meaning: The admitted instance is eligible for invocation and may have zero or more active invocations within its declared concurrency constraints.
phases.entryAuthority: Step Composition authorizes invocation; the validator executes its specialized behavior.
constraints: The concrete Step defines whether the instance is single-use, reusable, sequentially reusable, or concurrently shareable.
Invocation activity is tracked distinctly from association count and instance identity.

phases.name: Quiescing
phases.meaning: Step Composition has stopped admitting new invocations and is reconciling, completing, or cancelling active work before a lifecycle change or release.
constraints: The concrete Step defines whether quiescence waits, cancels, drains, or applies another safe policy to active invocations.
No new invocation may be authorized while the instance is quiescing.
Quiescence does not erase already-produced results or evidence.

phases.name: RetainedForReuse
phases.meaning: The instance remains alive under Step Composition coordination but is not necessarily associated or currently executing, and may be reused if its readiness and reuse conditions still hold.
constraints: Retention for reuse is an explicit lifecycle choice, not an automatic consequence of ending an association.
The concrete Step defines the conditions and duration for retaining an idle instance.
Retaining an instance for reuse is distinct from retaining validation evidence.

phases.name: Released
phases.meaning: The instance is no longer admitted or usable by the owning Step, and its required instance-specific release procedure has completed or reached a separately recorded failure/uncertain outcome.
phases.entryAuthority: Step Composition coordinates release and records the outcome.
constraints: Released denotes successful completion of the required release procedure. A failed or uncertain release remains a separately represented unresolved lifecycle outcome and must not be labelled Released.
Any later replacement runtime instance receives a new validatorUnitIdentity.
Historical evidence may still refer to the released instance identity.

rules: An instance must satisfy the concrete Step's readiness criteria before Step Composition admits it for invocation.
The concrete Step defines required initialization, configuration, dependency availability, resource acquisition, and validation of operational prerequisites.
The concrete Step defines whether readiness is a one-time admission check or must be re-evaluated before individual invocations or after relevant changes.
Association establishment is permitted only for an instance admitted to the owning Step, consistent with the Association Contract.
Admission may be revoked or suspended by Step Composition when readiness is lost, a lifecycle failure occurs, or the concrete Step's policy requires it.
Revocation of admission prevents new invocation authorization but does not itself determine whether the instance is immediately released.
admissionAndReadiness.readinessFailure: A readiness failure is a lifecycle fact. The concrete Step defines whether to retry preparation, retain the instance for diagnosis, replace it, or release it; no universal retry or failure policy is imposed.

rules: An admitted validator-unit instance may exist without any active association when the concrete Step permits such retention.
One instance may participate in multiple associations only when the Association Contract specialization permits it.
Ending one association does not change the lifecycle state of the instance or terminate its other associations.
Ending the final association does not automatically release the instance; Step Composition applies the concrete Step's independent reuse/retention/release policy.
An association must not remain usable for new invocations after its effective end point, even if the instance remains admitted and ready.
Before releasing an instance, Step Composition must ensure that every association involving that instance has been ended or otherwise invalidated under the Association Contract.
The association registry or retained association metadata may outlive the runtime instance when required for historical provenance; that metadata does not constitute a live association.
associationIndependence.coordinationBoundary: The Association Contract governs relationship identity, target binding, validity, and dissociation. This Lifecycle Contract governs the validator-unit instance. Neither contract transfers its authority to the other.

rules: Step Composition authorizes invocations only while the instance is admitted and satisfies the concrete Step's invocation-readiness conditions.
The concrete Step defines whether invocations may overlap, the maximum concurrency if bounded, reentrancy guarantees, synchronization requirements, and whether mutable internal state is permitted.
The concrete Step defines how active invocation count or equivalent in-flight activity is known reliably enough to prevent unsafe release.
A transition to quiescing prevents new invocation authorization before the release procedure proceeds.
The concrete Step defines how active invocations complete, drain, cancel, time out, fail, or transfer unresolved custody during quiescence.

A thrown exception or uncertain invocation outcome must be reconciled according to the behavioral/result and Step recovery contracts before the instance is considered safe to release, where that outcome may still involve instance-owned work or result custody.
Results already produced remain subject to their result/custody contracts and are not discarded by quiescence or release.
notMandated: A universal lock, reference count, lease, scheduler, or asynchronous task model.
A universal cancellation or timeout mechanism.
A universal rule that all validator units must support concurrent invocation.

rules: Reuse is permitted only while the instance remains admitted and satisfies the concrete Step's reuse/readiness conditions.
The concrete Step defines whether reuse is allowed across different associations, target scopes, or Step invocation boundaries.
The concrete Step defines whether instance state must be reset, reinitialized, isolated, or otherwise reconciled between invocations or association contexts.
An instance retained for reuse remains the same instance and retains its validatorUnitIdentity.
A replacement instance is a new instance and receives a new validatorUnitIdentity.
The concrete Step defines any retention limits, idle conditions, resource pressure responses, and release triggers.
Retention for reuse must not be inferred from the retention of results or evidence, and evidence retention must not be implemented by retaining the instance.
reuseAndRetention.reuseSafety: The concrete Step must ensure that state or context from one association or invocation cannot improperly affect another association or invocation. The required isolation, reset, or serialization mechanism is specialization-specific.

preconditions: Step Composition has stopped authorizing new invocations of the instance.
The instance is no longer admitted for new use.
All associations involving the instance have been ended or invalidated for future invocation under the Association Contract.
Active invocations and implementation-owned asynchronous work have been completed, cancelled, drained, or otherwise reconciled under the concrete Step's policy.
Any produced result or evidence whose custody is unresolved has been reconciled under its applicable custody/recovery contract to the extent required for safe release.
The concrete Step's implementation-specific release prerequisites have been satisfied.
execution: Step Composition coordinates the release operation through the validator-unit lifecycle mechanism defined by the concrete implementation.
The validator implementation performs its own resource shutdown/disposal mechanics as defined by its specialized contract.
Release completion, failure, or uncertain outcome is recorded distinctly; an attempted release is not automatically treated as successful release.
If release fails or its outcome is uncertain, the concrete Step defines whether the instance remains quarantined, requires reconciliation, or is considered unusable while cleanup continues.
postconditions: The instance is no longer eligible for association or invocation within the owning Step.
The same runtime instance identity is not silently reused for a replacement instance.
Historical validation results, invocation records, and association provenance remain subject to their independent retention policy.
Release does not imply deletion of result payloads, evidence records, or historical identity descriptors.
Release does not imply that all historical references to validatorUnitIdentity must be removed.
releaseContract.releaseFailure: A failed or uncertain release is not silently represented as Released. The concrete Step defines the state and recovery procedure for the instance and any resources whose release remains unresolved.

rules: Provisioning, initialization, readiness, invocation, quiescence, and release failures are lifecycle or execution facts distinct from validation outcomes.
The concrete Step defines whether a failed instance may be retried, reinitialized, quarantined, replaced, or released.
Replacing an instance creates a new validatorUnitIdentity; historical results remain attributed to the original instance.
An instance whose lifecycle state is unresolved must not be treated as ready or admitted for new work unless the concrete Step's reconciliation explicitly establishes that condition.
Lifecycle failure does not fabricate a validation result and does not rewrite results already produced.
Exceptions remain distinct from structured lifecycle or validation results unless a specialized contract explicitly defines a representation for them.
notMandated: Automatic retry, restart, replacement, or compensation.
Automatic conversion of lifecycle failures into validator results.
A universal recovery owner or quarantine implementation.

evidenceAndResultRetentionBoundary.principle: Validation results, invocation evidence, and historical association provenance may outlive the validator-unit runtime instance; their retention does not extend instance lifetime.
rules: The concrete Step defines the retention duration, ownership, representation, and release conditions of validation results and invocation evidence under the applicable result/behavioral contracts.
Any retained evidence that refers to an instance or association must preserve sufficient historical identity/provenance to remain interpretable after instance release.
Historical references to validatorUnitIdentity or validatorUnitAssociationIdentity do not imply that the referenced runtime instance or association remains active.

Evidence storage or retention must not hold runtime handles, object references, leases, or other resources in a way that unintentionally prevents instance release, unless the concrete Step independently requires that resource to remain alive for a different reason.
If result content directly depends on instance-owned resources, the concrete Step must define how that content is materialized, detached, or otherwise made valid before those resources are released.
Release of an instance must not delete, mutate, or invalidate already-produced result content that the Step's retention policy requires to preserve.
The concrete Step may release historical evidence before, at, or after instance release according to its own retention policy; neither lifetime is universally required to contain the other.
minimumHistoricalAttribution: validatorUnitAssociationIdentity where the result was produced under an association
associationTargetIdentity where required to interpret the result scope
validatorInvocationIdentity as defined by the behavioral contract
nonImplications: Retained evidence does not imply a live validator instance.
A released validator instance does not imply expired evidence.
No active association does not imply that the validator instance has been released.
An active validator instance does not imply that any validation evidence must be retained.

explicitNonGoals: No mandatory validator-unit lifecycle for Steps that do not select a validator unit.
No universal lifecycle state enum or fixed linear state machine.
No universal object construction, factory, dependency injection, pooling, ownership, or disposal mechanism.
No universal thread, task, scheduler, lock, reference-count, lease, or concurrency implementation.
No universal association topology or rule that an instance must have an association while alive.
No coupling of validator instance release to evidence expiration or historical association metadata deletion.
No requirement that a released instance remain alive to answer historical queries.
No transfer of lifecycle authority to an SPU because it is an association target.
No Pipeline-wide lifecycle manager or central mediator.
specializationRequirements: Define the concrete provisioning/acquisition mechanism and the identity assignment point for validatorUnitIdentity.
Define initialization/preparation requirements and readiness criteria.
Define the admission decision and the conditions under which admission may be suspended or revoked.
Define whether the instance is single-use, reusable, shareable, or concurrently invocable, including required isolation guarantees.
Define whether an instance may remain alive with no active associations and the policy for retaining it for reuse.
Define how active invocations and implementation-owned asynchronous work are tracked and reconciled before quiescence/release.
Define the dissociation coordination required before instance release, consistently with Step_Supporting_Validator_Unit_Association_Contract.json.
Define implementation-specific shutdown/release operations and how failed or uncertain release is represented and recovered.
Define which produced results/evidence must be detached from instance-owned resources before release.
Define result/evidence retention independently from instance lifetime and preserve the required historical provenance.
Define replacement behavior, ensuring a replacement runtime instance receives a new validatorUnitIdentity.
Define lifecycle behavior when the owning Step itself is quiesced, failed, or released.

references.relationship: Association identity, admission prerequisite, association validity/dissociation, and historical association provenance.
Step Composition authority over internal component lifecycle coordination and reuse/release decisions.
Owning Step boundary and Stage-facing lifecycle containment.
SPU boundary when it is an association target; no transfer of validator lifecycle authority.
Step-level retention and composition boundary for validation results.
Validator-unit behavioral capabilities, invocation, and result semantics.
Framework-level lifecycle coordination invariants refined by this specialized Lifecycle Contract; component-specific phases, resources, and custody remain authoritative.

openDesignDetails: Define the concrete validator-unit identity and invocation identity fields in the behavioral contract.
Define the exact validator result ownership and detachment requirements before instance release.
Define the concrete Step's lifecycle policy for validator instances when the Step invocation ends but the Step instance remains alive.
Define whether validator instances may be shared across concurrent Step invocations and the required isolation/concurrency guarantees.

frameworkCoordination.conformance: This contract specializes the shared Step Composition coordination invariants. Where the shared contract defines only conceptual identity roles or lifecycle distinctions, this document supplies the component-specific identity names, semantics, mechanics, and constraints.
frameworkCoordination.precedence: The common contract governs cross-cutting Step Composition coordination invariants. This specialized contract governs component-specific behavior and mechanics. Neither contract changes the component pattern?s distinct behavioral result semantics.
